promise: Change the language without losing the application.
audience: Developers rebuilding a whole application in another language or runtime.
trigger: Use when behavior, data, interfaces, and deployment must survive a whole-app migration.

modes.name: Inventory
modes.when: The source app must become a rebuildable specification.
modes.output: Observed surfaces, sequenced story cards, data/interface contracts, and acceptance criteria.

modes.name: Rebuild
modes.when: A story’s prerequisites and acceptance are known.
modes.output: An idiomatic vertical slice with unit and real-surface evidence.

modes.name: Verify
modes.when: Builder-created checks need an independent challenge.
modes.output: Source-derived parity findings, bounded reopen decisions, and retained unresolved cases.

examples.title: Preserve the failure path too
examples.brief: A fictional terminal editor is migrating languages; its save dialog preserves an unsaved buffer after a write failure.
examples.before: Translate the save function and count a successful unit test as parity.
examples.after: Observe the source failure state, put buffer preservation and recovery in the story, write the terminal probe first, then implement in target idioms.
examples.why: The observable contract includes failures, state, and recovery—not the source language’s line structure.

boundaries: The source remains read-only. Keep data migration and rollback explicit; code parity alone cannot establish data safety.
The optional Gene-Migration graph, ledger, Forge tool, and Amplifier are not required to install this method.
A ledger fitness curve measures declared completion, not independently established behavioral parity.

verification.name: Ledger ratchet and sequence detector
verification.evidence: Builder/verifier state regressions rejected and synthetic fixture curve read. These are fixture mechanics, not an app migration or behavioral parity measurement.
verification.expected: The stated scope passes; no broader result inferred.

verification.name: Executable graph syntax
verification.command: dot -Tsvg pipelines/inventory.dot -o /dev/null; dot -Tsvg pipelines/migrate.dot -o /dev/null; dot -Tsvg pipelines/verify.dot -o /dev/null
verification.evidence: All three retained graphs parse. No graph/orchestration changes or paid pipeline execution.
verification.expected: The stated scope passes; no broader result inferred.

verification.name: Portable packaging and install
verification.command: python3 scripts/capability.py build; python3 scripts/capability.py check; python3 scripts/capability.py doctor; python3 scripts/capability.py install --dest <temporary-parent> (twice)
verification.expected: Byte-identical canonical ZIP and isolated idempotent install.
verification.evidence: All operations passed. No runtime activation or effectiveness measured.

verification.name: Skill discovery metadata
verification.expected: Valid required frontmatter, naming, and complete scaffold.
verification.evidence: Skill is valid. This is a structural check, not a behavioral benchmark.

sources.role: Primary history and engine retained; methods consolidated behind the canonical portable entry.

evidence_summary: Retained graph syntax, ledger ratchet and sequence fixtures pass, and the portable install is checked. They validate orchestration mechanics; this release does not claim a newly completed app migration or production cutover.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Change the language. Preserve the experience.
marketing.lead: A whole-application migration skill. Observe how the source behaves, turn it into sequenced stories, and rebuild one complete slice at a time with data, failure and recovery checks.

benefits.title: Capture the app people use
benefits.body: Inventory commands, screens, hidden state, errors and persistence instead of translating files line by line.

benefits.title: Rebuild in the target’s idioms
benefits.body: Use source-derived acceptance criteria while respecting the target language and host architecture.

benefits.title: See what is actually complete
benefits.body: Keep implemented, independently verified, blocked and cut over as separate states.

walkthrough.title: Inventory the source
walkthrough.detail: Keep it read-only and describe observed capabilities as dependency-ordered stories with testable criteria.

walkthrough.title: Rebuild a vertical slice
walkthrough.detail: Write target checks and a real-surface probe first; include data handling and recovery.

walkthrough.title: Verify and plan cutover
walkthrough.detail: Challenge behavior against the source, preserve failures and record migration and rollback status.

use_when: A whole app must move to a different language or runtime.
A rewrite needs source-based acceptance rather than visual resemblance.
Data compatibility and failure recovery must survive the move.
not_for: A guarantee of parity from a green ledger or unit test alone.
An implicit data migration or permission to cut over a production system.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Migrate to inventory this fictional terminal editor for a Rust rebuild. Keep the Python source read-only. Start with open, edit, save and failed-save recovery; write dependency-ordered story cards and acceptance probes before implementation.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional story: recover from failed save
Given: edited buffer and unwritable destination
When: save fails
Then: buffer remains; reason is visible; retry is possible
Depends on: editor state and file boundary
Evidence: source observation + target terminal probe
State: inventoried; target implementation pending
marketing.proof_summary: Retained graph syntax, ledger ratchet and sequence fixtures pass, and the portable install is checked. They validate orchestration mechanics; this release does not claim a newly completed app migration or production cutover.
marketing.next_step: Bring the read-only source, target language and the surfaces that must survive.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.
